original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Accelerate the complete PR6338 idle-helper finite replay by exact pair-product reuse and minor extraction without temporary matrices, preserving its source main, scalar grid, full matrix transcript, guard counts and stdout.
scope_change_reason: The generic replay-runtime card is specialized to one immutable standard-library finite fixture. The predecessor theorem is cited rather than audited or extended.
bottleneck_link: Faster complete finite replays reduce verification latency without dropping a sample or a minor; this is verification tooling, not a supplier or kappa improvement.
stop_rule: Stop after the first verified original complete-command improvement; no further tuning.
evidence: Five alternating runs per side: baseline median 4.451049625 s, range 4.325743709–4.648084833 s; fast median 1.292453708 s, range 1.286811292–1.498913417 s. Zero failures and identical complete stdout. Matrix transcript and every original guard count agree across all 14,400 pairs, 230,400 assignments and 3,686,400 minors. See README.md for exact commands and limitations.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the same bounded evaluation adapter reduce the complete replay time for another explicitly pinned minor-based fixture?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The source theorem and coverage contract can differ even when a matrix loop looks similar.
open_questions.first_step: Select a distinct fixture, profile its full command, and derive its complete transcript and rejection contract before changing evaluation.
open_questions.blocked_by: No second fixture or general dispatch API is supplied; the adapter is deliberately scoped to PR6338.
